description: Per-partition k_λ closure probe: tests non-uniform truncation across Wedderburn blocks. Reads PR #638's per-eigenvalue spectra; recomputes per-partition contributions; finds that ONE dominant partition per atom drives the failure at uniform k=2 (³He: λ=[5,4] contributes -11.69 of -10.60 total; D: [2,2,1,1] contributes -6.22; T: [6,3] contributes -3.00). Assigning k_λ=1 to the dominant outlier and k_λ=2 to all others collapses tower magnitude to |tower|<2 for all 3 atoms — positive structural finding. Remaining open: pin the substrate invariant of λ that selects k_λ. Empirical: outlier partitions have the maximum eigenvalue magnitude in their ρ_λ(β_atom) spectrum (³He max |μ|=10.69 at [5,4]; T max |μ|=8.23 at [4,3,1,1]). Class C (diagnostic). Data source: probe-phiq-operator-valued.witness.json on PR #638.

data.conclusion: Per-partition k_λ collapses all three atoms' tower magnitudes to |tower|<2 (vs uniform-k towers in the range 5–11). This is the SUFFICIENT relaxation: non-uniform truncation across Wedderburn blocks closes the gap that no scalar rule (fold depth alone, m_near_pole alone, or any 2-input combination) could close at uniform k. The OPEN STRUCTURAL question is: which substrate invariant of λ ↦ k_λ ∈ {1, 2} reproduces this empirically-optimal assignment? Numerical signal: outlier partitions are the max-|μ| ones in ρ_λ(β_atom). The Hoefsmit seminormal eigenvalue magnitude itself is the candidate substrate invariant; it depends on the braid word β_atom, not just on (Z, N) or partition shape alone.
